svg.title: Anyon fusion
svg.text: Two anyons fuse into 1 (nothing) or ψ (a fermion). Which one depends on how they were paired.
1. Make a pair of σ anyons from empty space
2. Bring the two back together and fuse them
4. Now make two pairs from empty space
5. Fuse one anyon from each pair
A pair made from nothing carries total charge 1, which means nothing.
It fuses back into 1 with probability 100%, and into ψ with 0%.
1000 times 1 and 0 times ψ: the pair remembers that it came from nothing.
Each pair still carries total charge 1 on its own.
These two share no history: 1 with probability 50%, ψ with 50%.
Fusion 10 gave 1. So far 4 times 1 and 6 times ψ.
Fusion 100 gave ψ. So far 42 times 1 and 58 times ψ.
Fusion 1000 gave ψ. So far 481 times 1 and 519 times ψ.
One pair per qubit, plus one pair that keeps the total charge even. How a pair fuses is its bit.
σ: one anyon. 1: nothing is left. ψ: one fermion is left.
Computed in this run of BasicFusion.fsx (Ising anyons): Examples 2 to 4, plus the two-pair fusion via F-moves.
